stem: The domain of the function $f(x)=\frac{x+{=p}}{x-{=q}}$ is $R-\{c\}$. Find the value of $c$.
solution: The domain is R minus the set of zeroes of the denominator, so put the denominator equal to zero: $x-{=q}=0$.
$x={=q}$, so the denominator is zero only at $x={=q}$.
notes: Basic: one linear denominator. Numerator zero is at -p, never equal to q in sign confusion cases except none; fine.
